title: @latest tag points to dev version instead of stable version
body:
### What happens?

The [@latest](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/latest) tag on npm currently points to [1.29.1-dev132.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/1.29.1-dev132.0) instead of [1.29.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/1.29.0). 

It seems very likely that the wrong tag was updated by accident, since [@next](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/next) still points to [1.29.1-dev131.0](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/1.29.1-dev131.0).

### To Reproduce

Visit any of the referenced links.

comments.author: mbostock
comments.body:
To clarify, the `@latest` tag is what is installed by default if you run the following command:

```
npm i @duckdb/duckdb-wasm
```

Currently this means that when people install DuckDB-Wasm via npm, by default they get `1.29.1-dev132.0`, which was released two months ago, and is neither the latest stable or the latest stable release. I don’t think this is what you intend, but the download stats show that this version is indeed [quite popular](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm?activeTab=versions) and 20 times more popular than your `@next` tag.

Can you please run this command to fix your npm dist tags as I noted [back in January](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb-wasm/issues/1591#issuecomment-1908595801)? It takes just a second and will ensure that users get the latest stable version by default.

```
npm dist-tag add @duckdb/duckdb-wasm@1.29.0 latest
```

comments.author: mootari
comments.body: @carlopi Can we assist in any way to help resolve this issue?

comments.author: mbostock
comments.body: It has been almost a year since the last stable release 1.29.0 (October 7, 2024), and the `latest` tag is still pointing to an arbitrary unstable version (1.29.1-dev132.0) that is five months old (April 8, 2025). Can we get an update here, please? Will there be a stable release soon? Can you please repoint the `latest` tag to the last stable release 1.29.0? Or if you are no longer doing stable releases, can you point to the latest release instead of using a `next` tag? Thank you.

comments.author: mootari
comments.body: [@next](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/next) is now pointing to the latest stable release 1.30.0, while [@latest](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@duckdb/duckdb-wasm/v/latest) points to a version 1.29.2 that has been deprecated with the message "Security breach". 🤔

comments.author: carlopi
comments.body: Thanks for checking, @latest should also be re-pointing to 1.30.0, going to change that.

comments.author: azu
comments.body:
Just to confirm, is the DuckDB wasm extension not affected by this vulnerability and safe to use?

For example, when using the spatial extension from `@duckdb/duckdb-wasm` with a query like the following, it downloads the wasm file from a URL like this:

```
INSTALL spatial;
```

Downloaded wasm URK: https://extensions.duckdb.org/v1.1.1/wasm_eh/spatial.duckdb_extension.wasm

Is it correct to understand that this wasm file is not specifically affected?

--- 

📝 Since many people will likely see the article at https://socket.dev/blog/duckdb-npm-account-compromised-in-continuing-supply-chain-attack and search GitHub, I recommend pinning an announcement issue.

comments.author: mootari
comments.body: @azu The upload of those extensions appears to be managed through the [duckdb/duckdb repo](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb). I don't think they would have been affected by the advisory, but if you're concerned I suggest opening an issue there.

comments.author: carlopi
comments.body: @azu: extensions are NOT effected, those are build, signed and distributed directly by DuckDB Labs, and have a different distribution models than `npm` packages.

comments.author: mootari
comments.body: @carlopi I'm afraid this still seems to be an issue. `@latest` still points to 1.30.0, while `@next` points to 1.31.0.
